observation: Actually viewed all 120 whole-scene source frames through four bound JPEG pages, all 120 native-derived crops of each original hand through sixteen JPEG contact pages, all 285 detector boxes across all 120 candidate frames through eighteen native-derived JPEG contact pages, the original 25-example candidate sheet, native whole frame 119 and two wider native context crops from frame 108. Compared actual 768P input first frame and original P03 back-view artwork. The same one illustrated woman remains strictly back-facing, with stable silver hair, beret, blue butterfly ornament, feminine white/deep violet/gold dress, white legwear and purple boots. Both original resting hands stay attached to the correct sleeved forearms on the railing; no extra limb, palm reversal or changing wrist anatomy observed. Fingers overlap in the resting side view; not a claim of independently counted visible fingers in every frame. Water ripples, small hair and ribbon movements and fixed camera remain continuous. No head turn, eye/face reveal, added person, real face, reflection of people or scene cut observed. Detector boxes show trees, distant building/roof textures, stone pavement and a rusty railing junction; the two small distant clusters and right-edge brown/white cluster were checked in wider frame-108 context. No visible character eyes in this back view; no eye restoration needed. Original native source accepted, all original five seconds / 120 native frames retained. Assistant image-sequence review, not human continuous playback or formal film approval.
